title: A Parish for the Inheritance
premise: Bram Okonkwo, a night dispatcher who has spent years erasing herself from every record she can, receives two letters the same week: one from a dying man confessing to a hit-and-run twelve years ago, and one from an anonymous sender promising 'the rest of the story' if she can produce a witness the prosecution insists is dead. As Bram follows the letters through a decaying river parish, she discovers the witness is a woman she already knows from the taxi radio — a fare she has driven for months without ever seeing her face. The letters were bait, sent by the witness herself, who needs Bram's invisibility skills to smuggle her into court alive. In the trial's final hours, Bram must choose between remaining unseen and standing up as the found family the witness never had, ending with Bram testifying under her own name for the first time in her adult life.
about_author: Ivo Underhill is the pen name of a former emergency-services dispatcher who writes mysteries set in the small hours of working-class cities. They live near a river, keep a scanner radio out of habit, and maintain that the most honest conversations happen between 2 and 4 a.m.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Postmark
chapters.summary: Bram, working a slow night shift, opens two letters addressed in the same handwriting: a confession to a twelve-year-old hit-and-run, and a promise of 'more' if she finds a witness named Ada Voss, officially dead since the accident. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: unease — the letters know things only someone from her old parish could know.

chapters.title: The Fare Who Never Speaks
chapters.summary: Bram realizes the confession writer is Mr. Halloran, a retired parish clerk, and begins retracing the night of the accident. Meanwhile a recurring radio fare, 'the woman at the pharmacy bench,' books rides she never takes. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: creeping recognition — the past is not past, it's on hold.

chapters.title: What the River Parish Keeps
chapters.summary: Bram visits Halloran, who is dying and terrified, and learns the victim's family is about to win a civil trial — unless a witness surfaces. Someone ransacks Halloran's flat hours after Bram leaves. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: guilt; her questions may have painted a target on a dying man.

chapters.title: Dead Women Don't Book Rides
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing dispatch logs, Bram proves the silent fare's pickup points match Ada Voss's old addresses. She sets a trap with a decoy booking. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into fear — she's being watched as carefully as she watches.

chapters.title: Ada, Alive, and Angry
chapters.summary: The trap works: Ada Voss appears, scarred, furious, and armed with the second letter's remaining pages. She confesses she staged her death to survive the man who drove the car — a man now a respected judge's aide. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: confrontation; Bram must earn a stranger's trust in a single night.

chapters.title: The Price of Staying Invisible
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Ada's POV: the accident, the cover-up, and the years of erasing herself. She explains why she chose Bram — the dispatcher who once, unknowingly, sent a cab that saved her. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: grief and the cost of survival; invisibility as a slow death.

chapters.title: Halloran's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Halloran dies, but his parish ledger surfaces, mailed to Bram before his death, naming the driver and the men paid to bury the truth. Someone breaks into the dispatch office looking for it. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve; the paper trail is now a lifeline.

chapters.title: Nine Days to Verdict
chapters.summary: With the trial looming, Bram plans Ada's extraction from a safehouse to the courthouse, using taxi routes as cover. The driver's men close in; a decoy cab is run off the road. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: rising tension; every skill she used to disappear must now be inverted to bring someone into the light.

chapters.title: The Longest Fare
chapters.summary: The climax: the night before testimony, Bram drives Ada through a gauntlet of watchers, outmaneuvering them via the river service roads she knows by heart. Cornered at the parish bridge, Bram steps out, names herself, and buys the escape with her own exposure. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: sacrifice — invisibility traded, deliberately, for someone else's survival.

chapters.title: A Parish for the Living
chapters.summary: Ada testifies; the driver and his paymasters fall. Bram, now publicly visible, is offered her old parish back — and chooses instead to build a new one: Ada, the dispatch office, the found family of the night shift. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: resolution and quiet hope; she was never invisible, only unclaimed.
